title: ～ないと — if you don't ～, then ～ (so you must ～)
summary: Means 'if you don't ～, something bad will happen' and shows that one must do it. Add と to the ない form. The second half gives the consequence or the needed action.

body.p: 急がないと電車に遅れる states a condition and its result. A sentence cut short, as in もう帰らないと, means 'I have to go home' and explains one's situation.
More conversational than ～なければならない. ～ないと is often left hanging with だめだ or いけない omitted. For politeness use ～ないといけません or ～なければなりません.

examples.ja: 急（いそ）がないと、電車（でんしゃ）に遅（おく）れる。
examples.tr: If we don't hurry, we'll miss the train.

examples.ja: 薬（くすり）は食後（しょくご）に飲（の）まないと、効（き）かない。
examples.romaji: Kusuri wa shokugo ni nomanai to, kikanai.
examples.tr: If you don't take the medicine after meals, it won't work.

examples.ja: もう帰（かえ）らないと、母（はは）に叱（しか）られる。
examples.romaji: Mō kaeranai to, haha ni shikarareru.
examples.tr: If I don't go home now, my mother will scold me.

pitfalls: A good outcome cannot follow it: 勉強しないと合格する is wrong.
With superiors use a polite form; ending with 帰らないと alone sounds casual.
